title: Vrijshyam v. State of U.P.
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Sunita Agarwal, J. and Vikram D. Chauhan, J.
disposition: Writ disposed; petitioner directed to file s.127/cl.6.5 appeal within three weeks; recovery citation stayed eight weeks or until the stay application is decided, whichever is earlier.
headnote: A recovery citation on a final assessment is to be challenged under Section 127 of the Electricity Act, 2003 read with Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. Without entering the merits, the Allahabad High Court disposed of the writ, directed the petitioner to file that appeal within three weeks, required any stay application to be decided by a reasoned speaking order preferably within two weeks and the appeal preferably within six weeks, and stayed the citation dated 28.2.2022 for eight weeks or until the stay application was decided, whichever was earlier.
facts: The petitioner, Vrijshyam, filed a writ petition in the Allahabad High Court challenging a recovery notice and citation dated 28 February 2022 issued by the Executive Engineer, Vidyut Vitran Khand-I, Fatehpur. Counsel for the distribution licensee appeared. After a brief hearing, the petitioner's counsel agreed to challenge the final assessment by statutory appeal and asked only for interim protection until a stay application in that appeal was decided.

holding_units.topic: appeal against final assessment as alternate remedy
holding_units.holding: A recovery citation founded on a final assessment is to be challenged before the competent authority under Section 127 of the Electricity Act, 2003 read with Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. Without entering the merits, the Court disposed of the writ, directed the petitioner to file that appeal within three weeks, required any stay application to be decided by a reasoned speaking order preferably within two weeks and the appeal preferably within six weeks, and directed that the citation dated 28.2.2022 not be pressed for eight weeks or until the stay application was decided, whichever was earlier.
holding_units.flag: The Court named the statute as the 'U.P. Electricity Act, 2003' and paired s.127 with Clause 6.5 without a sub-clause or a finding that the assessment was under s.126.

principle_tags.application: The writ challenging the recovery citation was disposed of without merits and the petitioner was directed to file a Section 127 appeal before the competent authority within three weeks.
Clause 6.5 of the Supply Code was read with Section 127 as the appropriate statutory remedy in place of the writ.
The 28.2.2022 recovery citation was not to be pressed for eight weeks or until the stay application in the statutory appeal was decided, whichever was earlier.

not_decided.point: Merits of the final assessment and the recovery citation dated 28.2.2022
not_decided.note: The Court expressly declined to enter the merits and relegated the petitioner to the statutory appeal.
